items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: I eventually gave to Walt Gower, who plays clarinet for the Mother's Boys in Detroit.

ctx.x: Kind of a chaperone. Sorry, I find that funny. He was a notorious tightwad. Never spent any money. But one time he did give me a clasp for my necktie, which I eventually gave to Walt Gower, who plays clarinet for the Mother's Boys in Detroit. And he was very reliable on jobs. That is, he was always where he was supposed to be at the time he was supposed to be there. And never seemed to be paying much attention to the other musicians or what they were doing. And was extremely uncritical of other musicians.
How did it happen that he gave you a glass for a necktie?
